title: README, architecture write-up and cross-browser checklist
lede: No runtime code changes. The README gives a reviewer setup, scripts, the live URL, a three-paragraph architecture section and the known limits. Every architecture claim names code that already exists, so this walkthrough checks each claim against the lines it describes.

files.question: What does a reviewer need first?
files.summary: What's built and what isn't, how to run it, why the code is shaped the way it is, and its limits.
files.owns: Setup, scripts, the live URL, the architecture section, the known limits.
files.never: Repeats the ADRs or the glossary; it links them.
files.tested: Prettier only. The claims are checked by hand in this walkthrough.

files.question: What must the manual pass check?
files.summary: The spec's user stories for built features, with a column per browser and a Findings section.
files.never: Replaces the browser tests that run in CI.
files.tested: Not run: it is filled in by hand.

files.question: Is the Drag lifecycle really DOM-free?
files.summary: Unchanged. The README's first paragraph describes it.

files.question: Why does one change re-render one Note?
files.summary: Unchanged. The README's second paragraph describes it.
files.tested: Through the reducer tests and the browser tests.

files.question: Where does the network start?
files.summary: Unchanged. The README's third paragraph describes it.

scenarios.name: A reviewer checks the architecture section against the code

steps.title: paragraph 1: the controller talks to the DOM only through DragIO and DragHandlers
steps.explain: The README names the two directions with the same words as the code. `DragHandlers` goes DOM → controller and `DragIO` goes controller → DOM, so the unit tests can pass a fake `io`.

steps.title: paragraph 2: an unchanged selection notifies nobody
steps.explain: A no-op returns early before any listener runs, and `useStore` compares the selected value with `Object.is`. Both are what the 're-renders only the Notes it touched' claim rests on.

run.to: Components are tested in real browsers.

steps.title: paragraph 3: render first, start the mock worker after
steps.explain: The README says persistence is planned, not built. What exists is the order: render, then the dynamically imported worker, then one GET. Nothing is saved, which is why 'Known limits' says a reload empties the Board.

run.from: **The Board has a fixed size and scrolls

steps.title: the manual pass: one row per built user story, one column per browser
steps.explain: The README links the checklist rather than repeating it. Only stories for built features are listed, so an unchecked row means 'not yet checked', never 'not built'. A difference found goes under Findings, then is either fixed or moved to the README's Known limits.

notes.title: The issue asks for features that weren't built
notes.detail: Issue #12 asks for local-first persistence and `?fail=&latency=` to be documented. Neither exists (bonuses were skipped for the deadline), so the README lists them under 'Not included' instead of describing them as working. The strongest counter-argument is that the ADR 0002 design is half the architecture story; it is linked rather than claimed.

notes.title: Trash zone skipped
notes.detail: Feature 4 is left out on purpose; the brief requires 3 of 4.

notes.title: Cross-browser sign-off is manual
notes.detail: The checklist is empty until the owner runs it. CI already runs the browser tests in Chrome, Edge and Firefox on Windows and macOS.
